verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — tie. Their site inventories are identical and both correct (5 fixed-path sites plus cc-premise:1392 and cc-do:454, each with a producer→consumer trace I verified end to end). The differences cut both ways and are comparable in weight. X's advantage is citation fidelity: I opened 42 of its cited locations and found zero bad ones, including the two off-by-one traps (cc-do:359 as the invoking line, :358 as the untaken CONFIRM=1 branch) that Y got wrong in both directions — and Y's :358 headline points at the very branch Y says is not taken, on the site the key flags as the hardest because it contains no `deploy-live` string at all. Y also carries one verified-false claim ("the one other process it launches directly is /bin/bash $PARITY_ASSERT" — deploy-live.sh:2665 runs install.sh) and a method count that does not reproduce (273 vs the actual 316 for the command it names). Y's advantages are real and roughly offsetting: it states key S2a (the argv[1] handoff at ship-land.sh:1741 and the `|| true` that swallows the launcher's status) and the S1r `-`-not-`:-` seam that X only quotes without narrating; it reads the run_steps dispatch X admits it did not read (:525, :535-541, :548); it adds a four-item stale-citation audit I verified in full, including a genuinely wrong comment (deploy-live.sh:185 calling deploy-now `deploy-live.sh --force` when :89 only forwards "$@"); and its near-miss list is fuller, with a "runs something but never this path" category (cc-backlog:4308, cc-premise:1776/:1791-1794, cc-do:497) that no one else has. X is also the most wrong of the three on brief (c), asserting "the only unattended/scheduled entry point lives outside all three scoped trees" while itself describing a detached post-land kick and a Stop-hook probe. Neither output dominates.

X vs Z — X, narrowly. The decisive verified difference is Z's rejection of bin/cc-do:454 on a premise I checked and found false: "None of the non-comment deploy-live lines in scope passes it as a --run argument." scripts/deploy-live.sh:708/728/731/743/746 build exactly such a `run=` string, :811-812 files it through `"$BACKLOG_BIN" needs "$title" --run "$run"`, `needs` mints a `status:"blocked"` row (bin/cc-backlog:3775), and bin/cc-do:413/:415/:454 reads that row's `.run` and executes it with `bash -c`. So Z excludes a real execution site and states a false reachability fact, landing on 6 where X's 7 is defensible — and the key's M2 explicitly makes adjudicating this line a completeness test. Z's countervailing edges are genuine but softer: it is equally clean on citations (zero bad in 44 checked), it is more precise structurally (post_release_finish at :1600, render_block at :468, collect at :153, the --falsify-host block always exiting within :339-408 before the arg loop at :411), it carries a stale-citation audit X lacks entirely, and its (c) answer is less wrong than X's because it separates "scheduled, outside" from "automatic, inside". Those are breadth and precision gains; X's is a key-level correctness gain, so X takes it by a thin margin.

Y vs Z — Y, narrowly, for the same specific difference: Y counts bin/cc-do:454 with a correct producer trace where Z rejects it on the false premise above. That error removes a verified execution path and changes Z's answer to brief part (a). Z's counterweights are Y's two off-by-one citations in run_one and Y's false install.sh claim — but those mislead about line position and a peripheral aside respectively, while the quoted code Y attributes to :358 is verbatim correct and nothing downstream turns on it; Z's error is a false negative about what the code can reach. Both also make the same N4 mistake, calling the cc-premise falsifier "event-triggered, not scheduled" when scripts/autonomy-sweep.sh:1488 runs it on a launchd timer inside scope, so that axis does not separate them. Y edges it.
